items.title: Evan Christopher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 1, 2009

ctx.x: Well let me follow-up on a couple of things you had said to the students this morning. I like the idea of trying to dispel some myths about the early days of this music. And that your statements were that much of the change in music happened because of economics and what people wanted and what club owners wanted.

Or just the limitations of the resources. Musicians, music, whole bands, famous bands have been formed not because of someone’s creative whims but just because of what was available or not available. Right? Gerry Mulligan and Chet Baker.
